elements.text: Pilot conducted approach in structural icing conditions without activating wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system
Ice accumulation occurred on wing and horizontal stabilizer surfaces due to lack of deice system activation
Pilot failed to use appropriate landing performance speeds for weather conditions and airplane weight
Pilot used inaccurate occupant and cargo weights, influencing selection of slower-than-appropriate landing speeds
Pilot referenced Normal (non-icing) checklist, resulting in airspeed band indications that did not appropriately indicate stall speed
Pilot operated in icing-conducive environment for at least 15 minutes without activating ice protection systems
Failure to use ice protection systems was contrary to pilot training and standard operating procedures
Ice accumulation led to aerodynamic stall at a higher airspeed than normal
Stall occurred before aural stall warning sounded or stick pusher activated
Altitude was too low to recover from the stall
Airplane was properly certificated and equipped in accordance with federal regulations
Examination revealed no preimpact malfunctions or failures that would have precluded normal operation
Pilot's actions before takeoff were consistent with noncompliance with standard operating procedures
Recommendation to provide automatic alerting for ice protection system activation
Recommendation for improvements in pilot training regarding ice protection and stall avoidance
Installation of cockpit voice and data recorder benefited the investigation
